Dungeon-crawling is flipped around here: you work for the Dungeons Company and defend its treasures from invading adventurers who call themselves heroes. The game alternates between management, where you hire monsters, deal with staff problems such as strikes and keep traps in stock, and dungeon defense, where you study each party's stats and resistances and set up the most suitable traps and monsters against them.

Runs follow a roguelite structure, so each attempt differs, though some bonuses from your Master carry over. The office-comedy framing keeps the tone light. It is single-player with full controller support, suited to strategy fans who enjoy puzzle-like defense planning.
979070:
Old-age mayhem is the specialty of this sandbox from the designers behind Goat Simulator. You play an elderly, irritable retiree who has been thrown out of a retirement home in a near future with too few young workers to fund pensions. To qualify for free care, you take on risky challenges and roam the world gathering retirement tickets.

The game runs on dark, slapstick humor and a chaotic sandbox in which things go wrong in entertaining ways. You can play alone, team up online in co-op, or compete against other players. It suits fans of silly, unruly games who like experimenting and causing trouble, and anyone who enjoys the comic sensibility of Goat Simulator.
984800:
Building automated restaurants is the goal of this puzzle game. Each level gives you a kitchen to design: you place machines, connect them and program how they cooperate so that orders are prepared and delivered without a human cook. Puzzles test spatial planning, resource management and your ability to cope with problems such as shortages or kitchen fires.

There are several ways to play: a campaign of set levels, a contracts mode that moves you through the business world, and a sandbox test mode for free experimentation. Once a design is running, you watch it work, which makes success satisfying and failure informative. It is single-player, suited to players who enjoy engineering-style puzzles and optimizing systems.
990080:
The wizarding world of the Harry Potter books is revisited in the 1800s, well before the stories most people know, in this open-world action RPG. You play a student tied to an old secret that could divide the wizarding world. You attend classes, explore the castle and its surroundings, make allies and confront Dark wizards.

Along the way you cast and master spells, craft potions, find magical beasts, upgrade talents and customize your character. This version also includes the Haunted Hogsmeade Shop Quest, with an extra dungeon and a cosmetic set. It is single-player with full controller support, and it suits fans of the Harry Potter setting and anyone who likes exploring a large magical world.
990630:
Looking for purpose and a route back home, a small lost ember is stranded in a strange, puzzling place in this quiet adventure. You travel from the edge of a dark forest through wilderness dotted with ruins, strange creatures and other lost folk, working through obstacles and puzzles as you go.

Made by Hello Games, the small studio behind LostWinds, it centers on atmosphere and puzzle solving. The theme is hope: each stretch of the journey is about carrying a small light forward until you reach the last campfire. It is single-player with full controller support, suited to players who like reflective, story-led adventures with a calm pace.
994140:
Shadows are lethal in this first-person puzzle game. You work through its environments using lamps, beams and platforms to carve safe routes through the dark, since stepping into shadow means death. Lateral thinking is required, whether that means carrying a light source with you or repositioning one to light a gap you need to cross.

The setting is Lightmatter Technologies, led by its CEO Virgil, voiced by David Bateson, whose optimistic talk of a bright energy future runs through the game. The developers describe it as a love letter to first-person puzzlers. It is single-player and suits fans of that style who like light-based puzzles with a dark sense of humor.
735580:
11-11 Memories Retold follows two men on opposite sides of the First World War, starting in November 1916. Harry is a young Canadian photographer who signs up and heads for the western front, while Kurt is a German engineer who learns that his son has been reported missing and goes looking for him. Made by Aardman Animations with Digixart, the story moves between the two as their paths draw closer.

The game is a single-player narrative adventure with a painterly visual style, and its pace is slow and reflective rather than combat focused. It suits players who enjoy story-led games about ordinary people caught up in history, and who are happy to explore, take photographs and make quiet choices.
242820:
140 is a minimalist platformer from Carlsen Games built around music. Every moving platform, hazard and gap is tied to the beat of an electronic soundtrack, so reading the rhythm is as important as quick reflexes. The visuals are made of simple shapes and bright colors, and each level builds toward a boss encounter that leans heavily on timing.

It is a single-player game and fairly short, which makes it a good fit for an evening or two. Players who like tight, demanding jumps and want a platformer where the sound design shapes every challenge will get the most from 140. Steam achievements and cloud saves are included for those who want to track progress.
1701520:
Afterimage is a 2D action adventure with hand-drawn art, set among the ruins of a fallen fantasy world. You play as Renee, a young woman who wakes with no memory and sets out across a large, interconnected map, uncovering what happened to the land as she goes. Combat is quick and central to the experience, and you can shape your character through skill choices and weapon types.

The structure is close to a metroidvania, with branching paths, backtracking and areas that open up as you gain abilities. It is a single-player game suited to players who like exploring big maps, experimenting with builds and fighting demanding bosses at their own pace.
1904790:
Agatha Christie: Murder On The Orient Express retells the famous Hercule Poirot mystery in a modernized setting. A man is found dead on the snowbound luxury train, and Poirot must work out which passenger is responsible before the journey resumes. The game also adds Joanna Locke, a new character whose story runs alongside the classic case.

Play centers on searching rooms, examining clues, questioning suspects and linking evidence together to reach conclusions. It is a single-player detective adventure with a measured pace and little action despite the genre tags. It suits mystery readers and fans of investigation games who enjoy piecing together a case at their own speed.
40400:
AI War: Fleet Command is a space strategy game from Arcen Games in which humanity has already lost its war against artificial intelligence. Machine forces control most of the galaxy, and you start with a small foothold that has to grow without drawing too much attention. The AI reacts to how aggressively you expand, so every planet you take raises the threat against you.

It plays as a large-scale real-time strategy game with a heavy layer of long-term planning, and campaigns can run for many hours. You can play alone, or team up with friends in cooperative games online or over a local network. It suits patient strategy players who enjoy difficult, asymmetric challenges.
466160:
Arelite Core is a fantasy role-playing game that draws on classic console RPGs. You follow Karden, a blacksmith still learning his trade, who is pulled into a struggle against Talameq, an ancient being that has returned with plans to consume the world. Along the way he gathers companions and travels through towns, dungeons and open areas.

Battles are turn-based, and the game leans toward a traditional structure of exploration, story scenes and party management. It is a single-player game with a gentle learning curve, suited to players who are fond of older-style JRPGs and want a straightforward adventure rather than a sprawling one. Steam achievements and trading cards are included.
866140:
Arise: A Simple Story begins at the end of a man's life and sends him back through his memories, from childhood to old age. Each chapter is a large, dreamlike landscape built from one stage of his past, covering love, joy, loss and grief. The key mechanic lets you move time forward and backward within a scene, shifting the world around you to clear a path.

The game tells its story without dialogue and keeps a calm, steady pace built on light platforming and puzzles. It can be played alone or with a second person in local co-op, which suits couples or friends sharing a couch. It is a good pick for players who value emotional storytelling.
1119700:
As Far As The Eye is a strategy game about a nomadic tribe that has to keep moving toward a distant goal at the center of its world, known as The Eye. You gather resources, put up temporary buildings and assign tasks to your villagers, then pack everything up and travel on before conditions turn against you. Weather and other natural events add pressure along the way.

Turns are the core unit of play, and each run is generated differently, with skill trees and difficult decisions shaping how your people grow. It is a single-player roguelike suited to players who enjoy careful planning and resource juggling in shorter sessions instead of building one permanent city.
742520:
Astrologaster is a comedy adventure set in Elizabethan London and based on the real life of Simon Forman, a self-styled doctor who treated people by reading the stars. Patients arrive with all kinds of complaints, and you choose the astrological advice he gives them. Their later letters show how his guidance worked out, while Forman tries to gain recognition from the medical establishment of his day.

The game is story-driven and plays out mostly through reading and choices, with sung musical interludes adding to the humor. It is a single-player experience with no time pressure, well suited to players who like witty writing, historical oddities and short narrative games.
2114740:
Blasphemous 2 brings back the Penitent One, the silent warrior from the first game, who wakes in a new land and returns to battle The Miracle, the force behind the endless cycle of suffering. The world draws heavily on religious art and Spanish imagery, and it is packed with grotesque enemies, hidden paths and secrets to find.

It is a 2D action game in the metroidvania style, with exploration, backtracking and demanding boss fights. Combat is built around a choice of weapons that each change how you fight and which routes you can open. It is a single-player game aimed at players who enjoy tough, deliberate combat and a dark, detailed setting.
1555140:
Born of Bread is a lighthearted role-playing adventure starring Loaf, a golem made from flour and baked into life. Loaf sets off across a colorful world full of odd characters, with friends joining the party to help explore its regions and the mysteries they hold. The tone is warm and silly, and the writing aims for humor more than drama.

Battles are turn-based, with timed button presses during attacks and defense that reward attention instead of grinding. It is a single-player game with a relaxed pace, which makes Born of Bread a good choice for younger players or anyone who wants a cheerful RPG in the vein of classic paper-style adventures.
1623940:
Bramble: The Mountain King tells a dark tale shaped by Nordic folklore. You play as Olle, a young boy who goes searching for his sister in the land of Bramble, a place that looks like a fairy tale but hides cruel and frightening creatures. The journey moves through forests, swamps and mountains drawn from old Scandinavian stories.

The game is a linear, story-led experience mixing exploration, light platforming, simple puzzles and tense encounters with monsters. Some scenes are grim and disturbing, so it is better suited to older players. It is single-player only, and it fits those who like atmospheric adventures that can be finished in a few sittings.
274190:
Broforce is a side-scrolling shooter that parodies action movie heroes. You control a squad of muscle-bound commandos, each a spoof of a famous film character, as they blast through enemy territory to rescue prisoners and topple villains. Nearly everything on screen can be destroyed, so levels collapse and change as explosions tear through them.

Characters die in one hit, and rescuing captives swaps you to a new hero with different weapons, which keeps play fast and unpredictable. It works alone, but Broforce shines with friends in local or online co-op for up to four players, and there is also a competitive mode. It suits players who want loud, chaotic action in short bursts.
402060:
Californium is a first-person adventure inspired by the life and work of science fiction author Philip K. Dick. You play Elvin Green, a struggling writer in 1960s Berkeley whose sense of reality starts to break down. As the world around him shifts between versions of itself, he searches for the cracks hidden in his surroundings to find out what is really going on.

There is no combat, and the game is mostly about looking closely at each scene, solving riddles and following a strange, dreamlike story. It is single-player and fairly short. It suits players who enjoy surreal narratives and literary references, and who are happy with an experience driven by exploration rather than challenge.
241410:
CastleStorm combines castle building, physics-based siege combat and tower defense. Each side has a fortress, and you design your own from blocks and rooms, then try to knock down the enemy's walls with a ballista and other siege weapons. Meanwhile you send troops onto the field and can step in directly as a hero to fight on the ground.

The mix of aiming, building and unit management keeps battles varied and fairly quick. There is a story campaign for single players, plus multiplayer for playing with or against others. CastleStorm suits players who like lighthearted strategy with a hands-on action element and enjoy watching structures fall apart under fire.
8800:
Beyond the Sword, the second add-on for Sid Meier's Civilization IV, expands the turn-based strategy game in which you guide a nation from early history into the modern age. The expansion brings new civilizations, leaders, units and wonders, along with features such as espionage, corporations and random events that change the course of a game. A set of standalone scenarios offers different challenges as well.

The expansion keeps the classic Civilization loop of exploring, building cities, researching technology, trading and waging war, one turn at a time. Beyond the Sword is listed here for single-player play, and it suits strategy fans who want more depth and variety from a long-running favorite.
4560:
Company of Heroes is a World War II real-time strategy game from Relic Entertainment. The campaign follows American forces from the Normandy landings across France, with missions built around taking and holding key positions. You command squads instead of single soldiers, and units use cover, suppress enemies and level buildings as battles move through towns and countryside.

Resources come from capturing territory, which keeps fights moving across the map rather than turtling in one base. The game offers a single-player campaign and online multiplayer. It suits players who like tactical RTS games where positioning matters, and who want a grounded take on the war. This version also unlocks the updated release of the game.
9340:
Company of Heroes: Opposing Fronts is a standalone expansion to Relic's World War II strategy game. It adds two new armies, the British 2nd Army and the German Panzer Elite, each with its own units and style of play. One campaign covers the British push to liberate the French city of Caen, while the other places you on the German side during the fighting in the Netherlands.

It keeps the squad-based tactics, cover and territory control of the original Company of Heroes, with a single-player campaign and online multiplayer. Since it does not require the first game, it is an easy way in for real-time strategy fans who want more varied factions.
1619520:
Cross Blitz is a role-playing game built around collectible cards and deck building. You explore its world, take on battles against a range of opponents, and earn new cards as you go, slowly shaping a deck that fits the way you like to play. Crafting lets you create cards you need, and leveling up adds further options.

Combat is tactical and turn-based but moves quickly, with an emphasis on finding strong combinations between cards. It is a single-player game suited to players who enjoy card battlers and deckbuilders and want an adventure wrapped around them. Cross Blitz should appeal to anyone who likes tinkering with decks between fights.
1600:
Dangerous Waters is a modern naval simulation from Sonalysts that puts you in charge of ships, submarines and aircraft. You can command at the level of the whole task force from an overhead map, or move to individual crew stations such as sonar and weapons control and operate them yourself. Missions involve hunting submarines, protecting ships and coordinating different platforms together.

It is a detailed, demanding simulator with a slow and methodical pace, and learning the systems takes time. There is a single-player mode and multiplayer for crews of friends. Dangerous Waters suits players who enjoy realistic military simulations and want depth over spectacle.
934700:
Dead Island 2 is a first-person zombie action game set in a ruined version of Los Angeles. A virus has turned most of the city into the undead, and you play one of several Slayers who has been bitten but did not turn. You fight across well-known parts of the city, trying to learn what caused the outbreak and what is happening to your own body.

Combat is mostly melee and very gory, with weapons you can upgrade and modify, plus skill cards that change your abilities. You can play alone or team up with friends in online co-op. It suits players who want over-the-top zombie action with a dark sense of humor.
45740:
Dead Rising 2 moves the series to Fortune City, a Las Vegas style resort town overrun by zombies. You play Chuck Greene, a former motocross champion who must keep his young daughter supplied with medicine while clearing his name after being blamed for the outbreak. Events run on a clock, so you have to decide which missions and survivors to prioritize.

Combat is open and playful, as almost anything can become a weapon, and you can tape items together to make combination weapons. It can be played solo, or with a friend joining in co-op. Dead Rising 2 suits players who like zombie action with a sense of humor and some time management.
265550:
Dead Rising 3: Apocalypse Edition takes place in Los Perdidos, a California city overrun by the undead. You play Nick Ramos, a mechanic who has to find a way out before the military destroys the city. The open world is large and seamless, and you can loot, build combination weapons and vehicles, and save other survivors along the way.

This edition bundles the main game with its added story content. Combat is loose and chaotic, with hordes of zombies on screen at once. It can be played solo or with a friend in co-op, and it suits players who enjoy sandbox action, gleeful violence and experimenting with strange weapon combinations.
2014420:
Death Noodle Delivery puts you on the job as a new courier for a noodle delivery company in a grim cyberpunk city that seems close to falling apart. You ride a hoverboard around town to drop off orders, meeting the people who live there and slowly learning that the city hides something unpleasant beneath its neon surface.

Between deliveries you can modify your board and make unusual gadgets, including bombs shaped like cats. It is a single-player indie game with a casual pace and a quirky tone, mixing light action and role-playing with story. It suits players who like odd, small-scale adventures with plenty of personality.
9800:
Death to Spies is a World War II stealth action game told from the Soviet side. You play Semion Strogov, an officer of SMERSH, the counterintelligence service whose name gave the game its title. His missions take him behind enemy lines to steal documents, eliminate targets and uncover agents working against the Red Army.

It is played from a third-person view, and stealth is usually the best approach. You can take uniforms from enemies to move around more freely, hide bodies and choose between quiet and loud methods. It is a single-player game with a deliberate pace, suited to fans of classic stealth games who like planning their route through each level.
34410:
Death to Spies: Moment of Truth is the sequel to Death to Spies and continues the story of Soviet counterintelligence during World War II. You again take the role of a SMERSH agent, carrying out covert operations against German forces and enemy agents in a series of standalone missions.

Played from a third-person view, it focuses on disguises, careful movement and choosing when to act. Missions reward patience and planning, and loud approaches tend to go badly. It is single-player only and suits players who enjoy older-style stealth action with a historical setting. Anyone who liked the first game will find more of the same approach here, with new locations to infiltrate.
894020:
Deaths Door is an action adventure in which you play a crow whose job is to collect the souls of the dead. When a soul assigned to you is stolen, you have to chase the thief into a strange land where nothing dies and its creatures have lived far too long. The world is connected through a hub of doors, and the story has a dry, quiet humor.

It is viewed from an isometric angle and combines sword combat, ranged attacks, puzzles and challenging boss fights, in the style of classic Zelda games. Deaths Door is a single-player game with a moderate length, and it suits players who like tight combat and exploring a moody, handcrafted world.
820520:
Deceive Inc. is a multiplayer game about rival spies competing for the same prize. Each match drops several agents into a location full of ordinary people, and you can disguise yourself as anyone there to move around unnoticed. The goal is to reach the objective and get it out, while other players try to spot you and do the same.

You choose from a cast of agents with different gadgets and abilities, and matches mix social stealth with sudden firefights. You can play alone or in a small team with friends online, but there is no single-player mode. It suits players who like tense, competitive sessions built on bluffing and reading other players.
269650:
Dex is a 2D open-world role-playing game set in Harbor Prime, a futuristic city ruled by powerful corporations. You play Dex, a young woman who finds herself hunted and has to find out why. The city is open to explore, with side quests, factions and characters who can help or hinder you.

Problems can often be solved in different ways, through combat, conversation, stealth or hacking, which is shown as its own small action sequence inside cyberspace. You can also install augmentations to improve your abilities. It is a single-player game with a steady pace, suited to players who enjoy cyberpunk stories and RPGs with choices.
2481670:
Dino Path Trail is set on an American frontier where dinosaurs survived and still roam. You set off on a long, dangerous trip across varied regions to rescue your sister, who has been kidnapped. Along the way you deal with hungry predators, outlaws and harsh weather, and you have to hunt and manage supplies to stay alive.

It is a single-player survival roguelike, so runs are tough and setbacks are part of the experience. Each attempt plays out a little differently. Dino Path Trail suits players who like survival challenges and frontier settings, and who enjoy the tension of trying to keep going with limited resources.
248610:
Door Kickers is a tactical strategy game in which you command a SWAT team during police operations. Viewed from above, each mission shows a building with suspects and sometimes hostages, and you draw paths for your officers, set when they wait and which doors they breach. Then you watch the plan unfold and can pause to adjust it as things go wrong.

Missions are short and can be replayed to find cleaner solutions, and officers gain experience and better gear over time. It can be played alone or in online co-op. Door Kickers suits players who like planning and careful tactics more than reflex shooting, and who enjoy perfecting a plan.
1040420:
Dreamscaper is an action roguelite that follows Cassidy, a young woman dealing with loneliness and loss. At night you enter her dreams, fighting through shifting levels based on her memories and fears and collecting items that change how she fights. During the day she lives in the city of Redhaven, where she can meet people and form friendships.

The two halves feed into each other, since bonds built while awake unlock new strengths for the dream runs. Combat is fast and responsive, and dying sends you back to try again with progress carried over. It is a single-player game suited to players who like roguelites with a stronger focus on story and character.
1077970:
Dry Drowning is a visual novel with a detective story at its core, set in a bleak future city. You follow Mordred Foley, a private investigator with a questionable reputation and a past he would rather forget, as he looks into a string of brutal murders that take their inspiration from Greek myths.

Play involves reading, examining evidence and confronting suspects, catching their lies by presenting the right proof. Choices affect how the story ends. It is a single-player game with a slow, text-heavy pace and mature themes, so it suits players who enjoy dark crime fiction and visual novels with investigation built in.
25850:
Elven Legacy is a turn-based fantasy strategy game and the sequel to Fantasy Wars. Its campaign continues the earlier story, following the elves after a human mage discovers a dangerous secret tied to their ancient history. Missions move across hex-based maps where you command an army of different units and heroes.

Units gain experience and can be carried from one mission to the next, so keeping your best troops alive matters. Finishing missions quickly earns extra rewards, adding a layer of pressure. It offers a single-player campaign and multiplayer battles. Elven Legacy suits players who like classic war games with a fantasy setting and careful tactical play.
255340:
In Escape Goat 2, a puzzle platformer, you guide a small goat through a dungeon made up of single-screen rooms. Each room is a puzzle involving switches, moving blocks, traps and other machinery, and the goat has help from a mouse friend that can reach places and trigger mechanisms the goat cannot.

The challenge comes from working out the right sequence of moves and then carrying it out with good timing. It is a single-player game that can be played in short sessions, one room at a time. Escape Goat 2 suits puzzle fans who like clever level design and a mix of thinking and light action.
1110050:
Evans Remains is a short puzzle adventure that follows Dysis, a young woman who travels to a remote island after receiving a strange letter. The letter comes from Evan, a gifted boy who vanished years earlier and now appears to want her to find him. As she explores, she meets other characters and slowly learns what really happened.

Progress comes through a series of logic puzzles that block her path, mixed with dialogue scenes told in pixel art. It is a single-player game that can be finished in a few hours. It suits players who enjoy brain teasers and compact mysteries with a few surprises along the way.
312840:
Fahrenheit: Indigo Prophecy Remastered opens in a New York diner, where Lucas Kane comes out of a trance to find he has just killed a stranger. The story follows him as he tries to understand what happened, while detectives Carla Valenti and Tyler Miles work the same case from the other side. You switch between these characters, make choices in conversation and get through tense moments with timed button prompts.

Aspyr's remaster adds sharper HD textures and better controller handling, and it uses the full international cut of the original 2005 game. It is a single-player story game with light adventure elements, best for players who enjoy a cinematic thriller and do not mind trading deep mechanics for drama.
63900:
In Fantasy Wars, human kingdoms, orc clans, dwarves and elves fight over a classic fantasy world in turn-based battles. You move armies across a hex map, choose where to attack and defend, and lead heroes and regular troops through a series of campaign missions. Units gain experience as they survive, so keeping veterans alive between battles matters.

The pace is slow and thoughtful, with each turn giving you time to plan. There is a single-player campaign plus multiplayer for head-to-head matches. It suits fans of older hex-based wargames who want a fantasy setting, and its age shows in the visuals, which a modest price helps offset.
1137350:
Filament is a puzzle game set aboard a ship called The Alabaster, whose crew has gone missing. You guide a small craft that trails a cable behind it, and each puzzle asks you to wrap that cable around a set of pylons in the right order to light them up without tangling or blocking your own path. As you work through the ship, you learn more about what became of the people who were on board.

It is a single-player game with a calm pace and hundreds of puzzles that grow steadily harder. A hint system is available for the toughest ones. Filament is a good pick for players who enjoy logic puzzles and a quiet mystery in the background.
383870:
Firewatch takes place in 1989 in the backcountry of Wyoming, where a man named Henry takes a summer job as a fire lookout in Shoshone National Forest. His only regular contact is his supervisor Delilah, who talks to him over a handheld radio. You explore the forest on foot in first person, handle small tasks around the park and choose what to say to Delilah as strange events begin to pile up.

It is a single-player narrative game that takes a few hours to finish, with no combat and a strong focus on dialogue and atmosphere. Firewatch suits players who like a character-driven mystery and a relaxed walking pace with some tension along the way.
2910:
Fleet Command is a naval strategy game from Sonalysts, the studio behind several Jane's combat simulations. It puts you in charge of modern naval task forces in conflicts around the world, from frigates and destroyers to carriers, aircraft and nuclear submarines. You position ships, manage sensors, launch aircraft and decide when to commit weapons, with each scenario testing how well you use the forces available.

It plays as a real-time command simulation viewed from a tactical map and 3D views, rather than an arcade action game. Fleet Command is single-player only and best suited to players interested in modern naval warfare who are patient with older interfaces and enjoy careful planning.
821250:
Flotsam is a city-builder set on a flooded world where a small town floats across an ocean full of garbage. You steer that drifting settlement, send its residents out in boats to salvage wood, plastic and scrap, and turn what they gather into housing, food and clean water. Along the way you find sunken ruins, old factories and people in need of a home, which lets the town grow.

It is a single-player management game with a relaxed pace and a colorful style, where the main challenge is keeping your drifters fed and supplied while you keep moving. Flotsam fits players who like cozy builders with a light survival edge rather than heavy economic systems.
527230:
In For The King, a party of three adventurers sets out across the realm of Fahrul after its king has been murdered, in a strategy RPG with tabletop roots. You move your heroes across a hex map, visit towns, dungeons and encounters, and fight turn-based battles where actions succeed or fail on chance rolls that your stats influence. Runs are partly random, and losing can mean starting a new adventure.

You can play alone controlling all three heroes, or team up with friends online or on the same screen, with each player taking a character. It has the feel of a tabletop board game with roguelike difficulty, and it suits groups or solo players who enjoy planning around luck.
1170080:
Foretales is a story-driven card game in which a thief named Volpe has visions of the world coming to an end and sets out to change that outcome. Each chapter presents a situation, and you play cards representing people, places and skills to resolve it, choosing whether to fight, sneak, bargain or talk your way through. Your decisions change how the story unfolds and which ending you reach.

It is a single-player game with a thoughtful pace, mixing puzzle-like card choices with narrative. There is no deckbuilding grind; the focus stays on the story and the many ways to solve each scene. Foretales suits players who like card games and fairy-tale storytelling.
297060:
Freaking Meatbags is a comic strategy game where you play as robots sent to mine planets before their solar system blows up. To gather resources, you put captured humans, the meatbags of the title, to work, breeding them to combine traits that make them better at certain jobs. At night, hostile robots attack, so you also have to build turrets and defenses to keep your base standing.

The game mixes real-time base management with tower defense, and each level is a race against the clock. It is single-player only, with a comic tone and simple visuals. It suits players who enjoy light strategy with some juggling of tasks and do not want a long, complex campaign.
1347780:
Freedom Fighters is a third-person shooter set in a version of history where the Soviet Union has invaded the United States. In occupied New York, you play Chris Stone, a plumber who joins the resistance after his brother is taken. As the campaign goes on, Chris earns the trust of more fighters, and you can recruit them into a squad and give them simple orders to attack, defend or follow.

Originally released in 2003 by IO Interactive, the game is single-player and moves at a brisk pace, mixing street fights with sabotage objectives across the city. Freedom Fighters suits players looking for a classic squad-based action game with straightforward controls and a short, focused campaign.
243800:
In the combat racing game Gas Guzzlers Extreme, the cars carry machine guns, rockets and other weapons. You race around tracks while shooting rivals and grabbing pickups, earn money from wins and kills, and spend it on new cars and upgrades. Besides standard races, there are modes where the aim is to knock out opponents or fight in arenas instead of crossing the finish line first.

The pace is fast and loud, and it does not take itself seriously. There is a single-player career plus multiplayer and co-op modes for playing with others. It suits players who miss arcade car combat games and want quick, chaotic sessions more than realistic driving.
488730:
God's Trigger is a top-down action game about an angel named Harry and a demoness named Judy who team up to stop the Apocalypse. Each level is a series of rooms full of armed enemies, and you clear them quickly using guns, melee weapons and special abilities, such as teleporting or mind control. One hit can end a run, so planning a route and reacting quickly both matter.

You can switch between the two characters on your own or play in co-op, either on the same screen or online. The violence is graphic and the pace is very fast. It suits players who enjoyed games in the style of Hotline Miami and want a partner along.
858710:
Gravity Circuit is a 2D action platformer that takes inspiration from classic console series such as Mega Man X. You play as Kai, a war hero who fights rogue robots in a futuristic world. Instead of shooting, Kai relies on fast melee combat, punching and kicking his way through enemies, and uses a grappling hook to swing across gaps and pull foes close. Defeating bosses unlocks new abilities.

It is a single-player game with tight controls, bright pixel art and a fast but fair difficulty. Levels reward speed and skill, with secrets to find. Gravity Circuit suits players who loved 16-bit action platformers and want something that feels classic with a modern level of polish.
1311070:
Greak: Memories of Azur, a hand-drawn puzzle platformer, follows Greak, Adara and Raydel, three siblings who must escape their homeland of Azur as an invading force and its creatures spread across the land. Each sibling has different skills: one is nimble, one can float and use magic, and one is strong and carries a shield. You switch between them or move them together to solve puzzles and fight.

It is single-player only, and controlling all three at once can be demanding during combat and platforming. The pace is moderate, with exploration and some backtracking. Greak suits players who like adventure games with a storybook look and are comfortable managing several characters at once.
6850:
Hitman 2: Silent Assassin follows Agent 47, who has left his former life to work as a gardener at a church in Sicily. When the priest who sheltered him is kidnapped, 47 goes back to contract killing to get him back. The missions take him to locations such as Sicily, St. Petersburg, Japan, Malaysia and India, where he must take out targets in whatever way he chooses.

Released in 2002, it is a single-player stealth action game where disguises, careful planning and patience pay off more than direct fighting. You can complete missions quietly or loudly, but quieter approaches earn better ratings. It suits players who enjoy classic stealth and want to see an early high point of the series.
203140:
Hitman Absolution follows Agent 47 after he is betrayed by the Agency he once worked for. Hunted by both the police and former employers, he travels through locations such as Chicago while protecting a young girl named Victoria. Each level offers several ways to reach a target, using disguises, distractions and hiding spots, and the Instinct ability lets you see through walls and blend in when spotted.

It is a single-player stealth action game with a strong story and a more linear structure than other entries in the series. You can play cautiously or go loud, and score depends on how cleanly you work. Hitman Absolution suits players who like stealth with a cinematic campaign.
404680:
Hob comes from Runic Games, the studio known for Torchlight, and is a quiet action-adventure. You play a small hero in a red cloak who receives a powerful mechanical arm and sets out to heal a broken, mysterious world. Exploring reveals huge machines and hidden mechanisms, and using them reshapes the land itself, opening new paths. There is no dialogue; the story is told through the environment.

It is single-player, viewed from an isometric camera, and mixes exploration, platforming, puzzles and some combat. The pace is unhurried and rewards curiosity. Hob suits players who enjoy games in the style of classic Zelda titles and like piecing together a world without being told where to go next.
838110:
HyperParasite is a roguelite twin-stick game set in an alternate 1980s, where an alien parasite tries to take over humanity. On its own, the parasite is weak, so you take over the bodies of people you meet, each with their own weapons and abilities. There are 60 characters to unlock, and the ultimate goal is to work up the ladder, all the way to possessing the President.

Each run is randomly generated and can end quickly if you are careless, so it rewards quick reactions and choosing hosts well. You can play alone or with a friend in local co-op. HyperParasite suits players who like fast, replayable shooters with a sense of humor.
1172650:
INDUSTRIA is a first-person shooter that begins in East Berlin in 1989, near the end of the Cold War. You play as Nora, a researcher who goes looking for a missing colleague and ends up in a strange parallel world. There, a city is controlled by machines, and she has to fight her way through while gathering clues about the place and how it connects to her own.

It is a single-player linear campaign that takes a few hours to finish, mixing gunfights, exploration and story. The pace is measured, with an emphasis on mood over speed. INDUSTRIA suits players who enjoy atmospheric shooters in the vein of Half-Life and prefer a compact story.
1019590:
Lovely Planet 2: April Skies is a fast first-person shooter with a bright, cheerful look, sequel to the original Lovely Planet from 2014. Each level is a short obstacle course where you jump between platforms and shoot every enemy, often while dodging projectiles. Many levels require hitting targets in a specific order or before time runs out, so accuracy and movement are tied together closely.

It is a single-player game that rewards practice, with frequent restarts and the challenge of improving a run. Levels are brief, making it easy to play in short sessions. It suits players who enjoy precision platforming and speedrun-style challenges, more than story or exploration.
1933000:
Luna Abyss is a story-driven action-adventure from Kwalee Labs. You play Fawkes, a prisoner sent to a vast structure on the Moon called Luna. Bound by a prophecy that no one fully explains, Fawkes must travel through the depths of this place while serving a sentence. The game combines exploration with platforming and gunfights against enemies that fill the screen with projectiles.

It is a single-player game, so expect a focused campaign with a dark science-fiction tone. Combat leans toward dodging dense patterns of bullets, which calls for good reflexes. Luna Abyss suits players who like shooters with a strong atmosphere and movement-heavy combat, and who enjoy a story that leaves a few questions open.
1050370:
LUNARK is a pixel-art science-fiction platformer modeled on 1990s cinematic games such as Flashback and Another World. You play Leo, who gets caught up in a rebellion against an oppressive regime. Animation is rotoscoped for realistic motion, and you move through each location by running, climbing ledges, rolling and shooting enemies, while solving environmental puzzles along the way.

It is a single-player game with deliberate controls that favor careful movement over speed. Some jumps and fights can be demanding, but checkpoints keep frustration in check. LUNARK suits players who grew up with cinematic platformers or are curious about the style, and who enjoy a game with a clear story and handcrafted pixel visuals.
629820:
Maneater is an action RPG in which you play a bull shark seeking revenge on a shark hunter named Scaly Pete. Starting as a small pup in the bays of Port Clovis, you hunt fish, fight other predators and attack boaters along the Gulf Coast. Eating helps you grow, and you unlock new body parts and abilities that change how you fight. The whole story is narrated like a reality TV show.

It is a single-player open-world game with a comic tone and a loop of hunting, growing and taking on bigger challenges. The pace is relaxed between missions. Maneater suits players who want a silly, simple action game with clear progression.
64000:
Men of War: Assault Squad is a World War II real-time tactics game focused on skirmish battles. You choose one of several nations, including the Soviet Union, the United States, Germany, Japan and the Commonwealth, and fight across settings from European farmland to Pacific islands. You command infantry, tanks and artillery, and you can take direct control of a single unit to aim and drive by hand.

The game is very detailed, with ammunition, vehicle damage and line of sight all affecting fights. You can play alone against the AI, team up with others in co-op, or compete online or on LAN. It suits strategy players who want tactical depth and do not mind a steep learning curve.
204860:
Men of War: Condemned Heroes is a standalone entry in the series, a real-time tactics game set on the Eastern Front in World War II. You lead a Soviet penal battalion, made up of punished soldiers sent on dangerous missions. The campaign draws on real events, and you command small groups of infantry, use cover, capture vehicles and take direct control of units when precision matters.

It is a demanding tactics game, where losing a few soldiers can change how a mission plays out. Besides the single-player campaign, it supports co-op, LAN and competitive multiplayer. Condemned Heroes suits fans of earlier Men of War games who want a harder, story-focused campaign with a darker side of the war.
3130:
Men of War: Red Tide is a standalone expansion for the Men of War series, developed with Russian author Alexander Zorich. It follows the Soviet naval infantry, known as the Black Coats, as they fight in the Black Sea region during World War II. Missions mix large battles with small-unit actions, and you command infantry and vehicles while taking direct control of any unit when needed.

The game uses the series' detailed tactics model, where cover, ammunition and vehicle armor all matter. You can play the campaign alone or join others in co-op, LAN or competitive multiplayer. Red Tide suits players who already enjoy the Men of War formula and want a campaign centered on a less familiar front.
1061910:
In the rhythm-based first-person shooter Metal: Hellsinger, you play the Unknown, a half-human, half-demon who fights through the Hells to take revenge on the Red Judge. Shooting, reloading and dodging in time with the music boosts your damage and builds a multiplier, and the soundtrack grows louder as you keep the beat. Each level has its own track, with vocals from well-known metal singers.

It is single-player, with a campaign that can be finished in a few hours and challenges that extend replay value. The pace is fast, and staying on beat takes practice. Metal: Hellsinger suits players who enjoy shooters like Doom and want a twist that rewards a sense of rhythm.
1517180:
Mindcop is a detective game where you investigate a murder in a small town. As the Mindcop, you have the unusual ability to enter suspects' minds, which plays out as a real-time puzzle where you dig up hidden memories and catch people in lies. Between these sessions, you talk to residents, collect evidence and follow leads in whatever order you choose, building your case step by step.

It is a single-player game with a relaxed pace, though the investigation runs on a limited schedule, so you have to decide where to spend your time. Mindcop suits players who enjoy whodunnit mysteries and want a story game that also tests their puzzle skills.
415200:
Motorsport Manager puts you in charge of a racing team, from hiring drivers and engineers to designing and improving your cars. On race weekends, you plan practice and qualifying, then call strategy live during the race, deciding when to pit, which tires to fit and how hard drivers should push as weather and conditions change. Between races, you manage budgets, sponsors and car development.

It is a single-player management game that can be as deep as you want, with many seasons of play. Races can be sped up or followed closely. Motorsport Manager suits fans of motorsport who enjoy strategy and spreadsheets more than driving, and anyone who liked classic sports management games.
760060:
Mutant Year Zero: Road to Eden is a tactical game set on an Earth where humanity has collapsed. You lead a small team of mutants, including a duck named Dux and a boar named Bormin, out from their settlement, the Ark, to scavenge the dangerous Zone. Exploration happens in real time, and when a fight starts, the game switches to turn-based combat in the style of XCOM.

Stealth matters a lot, since you can pick off enemies quietly or set up ambushes before a battle. It is a single-player game with a fixed story, a measured pace and a fairly demanding difficulty. It suits players who enjoy tactics games and want more story and exploration between battles.
814360:
Mythic Ocean is a narrative exploration game set in an underwater world inhabited by gods who are about to create a new universe. You swim through the sea, meet these deities and talk with them, getting to know their personalities and helping them grow. The conversations you have and the advice you give shape which kind of universe they end up creating.

It is a single-player game with no combat and a gentle pace, relying on dialogue and exploration. There are several endings, which invites replays to see how different choices play out. Mythic Ocean suits players who enjoy cozy, story-focused games with an emphasis on relationships and a calm, colorful underwater setting.
366870:
Narcosis is a first-person survival horror game set at the bottom of the Pacific Ocean. You play an industrial diver in a heavy diving suit, trapped after an accident at an undersea facility. With only a flashlight, flares and a knife, you have to work your way back to the surface while watching your oxygen supply and dealing with what lurks in the dark, as panic begins to affect what you see.

It is a single-player game with slow movement and a heavy focus on atmosphere and tension rather than combat. It also supports VR headsets. Narcosis suits players who like short horror experiences built around isolation and dread, more than action and jump scares alone.
2017080:
Nickelodeon All-Star Brawl 2 is a platform fighter with characters from Nickelodeon shows such as SpongeBob SquarePants, Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles and Avatar: The Last Airbender. Matches take place on multi-level stages where you knock opponents off the screen, and each fighter has a distinct move set plus a Super attack that can turn a match around. There is also a single-player campaign with roguelike elements.

You can play against the computer, compete with friends locally or take your skills online. Matches are short and fast, and newcomers can pick it up while experienced players can dig into movement and combos. It suits fans of these shows and of platform fighters in general.
1634080:
Nocturnal is a 2D action platformer in which a warrior returns home to find the island shrouded in a deadly mist. Fire is the key to survival: your sword can catch flame from braziers and torches, and carrying that fire lets you burn enemies, light up the darkness and push through areas where the mist would otherwise harm you. Short challenges and puzzles are built around keeping the flame alive.

It is a single-player game that can be finished in about two hours, with a hand-painted look and fast combat. The difficulty is noticeable but fair. Nocturnal suits players looking for a compact action game with a clever central idea that they can finish in an evening.
1662480:
Nuclear Blaze is a 2D firefighting platformer from Deepnight Games, the studio of the lead developer behind Dead Cells. You play a firefighter sent into a secret government facility to put out a spreading fire. Armed with a hose and limited water, you spray flames, break through walls and watch for backdrafts and explosions, while rescuing the occasional trapped cat. Clues hint that more is going on inside.

It is a single-player game with a short campaign and an unusual focus on putting out fires instead of fighting enemies. The action is fast and satisfying, with fire spreading in realistic ways. Nuclear Blaze suits players who want something different from the usual action platformer.
581270:
Old Man's Journey is a puzzle adventure in which an elderly man sets out on a trip after receiving a letter. As he travels through hand-painted landscapes of hills, villages and coastlines, you help him by reshaping the scenery, pulling and pushing hills so that the layers line up and create a path for him to walk. Along the way, memories from his past reveal the story of his life.

It is a single-player game that takes a couple of hours to complete, with a slow, gentle pace and no fail states. There is no spoken dialogue; the story is told through pictures. Old Man's Journey suits players who want a short, reflective game with a lovely art style.
1297330:
Olija follows Faraday, a man who is shipwrecked and stranded in Terraphage, a strange and unfriendly land. He finds a legendary harpoon early on, and with it he sets out to help fellow castaways and find a way home. The harpoon is both weapon and tool: you throw it at enemies or surfaces and then pull yourself across to where it landed.

Olija is a single-player action adventure from Skeleton Crew Studio, published by Devolver Digital, drawn in sparse, moody pixel art. Combat is quick and tight, and the adventure is fairly short, so it suits players who like a compact, atmospheric game they can finish over a few evenings.
277700:
On Rusty Trails is a quick-reflex platformer built around a single idea: the world only tolerates things that look like it. Your character can switch form on the fly, and matching the right shape at the right moment decides whether a part of the level treats you as a friend or as a threat. Getting through a stage means changing your look constantly while running and jumping.

It is a single-player game from the small studio Black Pants, with short, demanding levels that reward practice and quick decisions. It suits platformer fans who enjoy trial and error, tight timing and a puzzle twist layered on top of the running and jumping.
1398100:
Orwell's Animal Farm adapts George Orwell's famous novella as an interactive story. The animals drive out the farmer and try to run the farm by their own rules, and you make the decisions that steer how that revolution unfolds, from who gets fed to how the pigs hold on to power. The text is supported by illustrated scenes, and different choices lead the story toward different outcomes.

The game comes from Nerial, the studio behind Reigns, and is played entirely solo at your own pace. There is no action or timing involved, so it suits readers, fans of the book and anyone who enjoys short choice-based stories with room for replays.
414700:
Outlast 2 is a first-person horror game set in the remote Arizona desert. You play Blake Langermann, a camera operator whose wife goes missing after their helicopter crashes near Temple Gate, a hidden settlement led by the preacher Sullivan Knoth, whose flock believes the end of the world is near. You cannot fight back, so you run, hide and sneak past the villagers while searching for her.

Your camcorder lights the dark with night vision, but its batteries run down, which adds steady pressure. It is a single-player game with a tense, often graphic tone, best suited to players who like intense survival horror and do not mind disturbing material.
1288410:
Outshine is an arcade action game where your keyboard is your weapon. Instead of aiming with a mouse or stick, you type words to move, dodge and attack as a glowing hero striking back at the forces that held them down. Stages are full of traps and enemies, and boss fights test how fast and accurately you can type under pressure.

Made by Belgian studio Fishing Cactus, it is a single-player game with online leaderboards for players who want to chase better scores. Runs are short and fast, so it suits confident typists, players who like score-attack games, and anyone looking for a playful way to sharpen their typing speed.
773740:
Overpass is a rhythm game played from behind the wheel. You drive along a futuristic road through a stylized city, and the track, the skyline and the obstacles all move in time with the music. Steering, drifting and hitting your timing on the beat are what carry you forward on this musical road trip.

It is a single-player game from the small independent Studio Bean, focused on mood and flow more than on racing against rivals. It suits players who like rhythm games and calm driving, and who enjoy music-led experiences with a strong visual style that can be played in short sessions.
289440:
Perimeter is a real-time strategy game from the Russian studio K-D Lab, first released in 2004. Bases are protected by energy shields, the perimeters of the title, and much of the fighting is about claiming and defending ground. You can reshape the terrain itself, raising and flattening land to make room for buildings, and your units can transform into different forms to suit the battle at hand.

There is a single-player campaign with a science fiction story, plus skirmish and multiplayer matches against AI or other people. It suits RTS players who want something less conventional than the usual base-and-army formula and who enjoy managing energy and territory.
289240:
Perimeter: Emperor's Testament is a standalone follow-up to K-D Lab's real-time strategy game Perimeter. It picks up where the first game's plot left off, with a large new single-player campaign, keeping the same core ideas: shield-protected bases, territory you reshape with terraforming, and units that can change form during battle.

Besides the campaign, it supports multiplayer matches against other players. It plays at a measured strategy pace that rewards planning over fast clicking. It is a good fit for players who finished the first Perimeter and want more of its story, or for RTS fans curious about an older and unusual take on the genre.
1383250:
In Please Fix The Road, a relaxed puzzle game, your job is repairing broken roads. Each level shows a small, colorful scene with gaps in the route, and you place road pieces to connect everything so traffic can get through. The solution only needs to work, not look neat, which keeps the mood light and forgiving.

It is a single-player game with a clean, minimal look and no time pressure, so you can play in short sessions and think at your own pace. It suits casual puzzle fans, younger players and anyone who wants a calm game to unwind with, rather than a stiff challenge.
19980:
Prince of Persia from 2008 is a reboot of the series by Ubisoft Montreal. A wandering adventurer meets Elika, a princess with magical powers, and the two set out to heal a land being swallowed by a dark corruption after an ancient evil god is released. You climb, wall-run and leap across ruins in a painterly, cel-shaded world, cleansing regions one by one.

Elika stays at your side and saves you from deadly falls, so the game is forgiving and keeps you moving. Combat is one-on-one duels. It is a single-player action adventure suited to players who enjoy acrobatic exploration and a relaxed pace.
13500:
The second game in the Sands of Time trilogy, Prince of Persia: Warrior Within takes a darker turn. The Prince is pursued by the Dahaka, an unstoppable guardian of the timeline, because he escaped the fate the Sands should have brought him. To change his destiny he sails to the Island of Time, where he travels between past and present to stop the Sands from ever being created.

It mixes acrobatic platforming and time-rewinding powers with a heavier, combo-based combat system and a grim tone. It is a single-player action adventure suited to players who want more fighting alongside their climbing and puzzles.
290320:
In Project Temporality, a third-person puzzle game, the trick is cooperating with yourself. You record a run of actions, then rewind and play alongside the earlier copies of yourself, which repeat what you did. Standing on switches, holding doors and dealing with obstacles all depend on how you layer these recordings in a futuristic test setting.

It is a single-player game from Defrost Games, built on their own engine, and leans more toward head-scratching puzzles than fast action. It suits players who like time manipulation ideas and do not mind planning, failing and rewinding a few times before a solution clicks.
512790:
Quern - Undying Thoughts is a first-person puzzle adventure in the tradition of Myst. You wake in a strange place and explore an island of old buildings, machines and gardens, piecing together what happened there from notes and clues while working out how its devices function. Many puzzle ideas come back later in new forms, so what you learn early keeps paying off.

It is a single-player game with no combat or time pressure, played at a slow and thoughtful pace. It suits fans of classic adventure puzzlers who like taking notes, exploring every corner and solving problems that connect across the whole map.
900270:
Reventure is a comedic pixel art adventure that hides 100 separate endings. The usual setup is there, a hero, a princess and a dark lord, but almost anything you do can end the story early, from careless jumps to odd decisions. Each ending teaches you something new about the small world, and finding them all means thinking creatively about every item and path.

It is a single-player game made of short attempts, so it is easy to dip into for a few minutes at a time. It suits players who enjoy jokes about game cliches, secret hunting and completion lists more than a hard action challenge.
418460:
Rising Storm 2: Vietnam is a multiplayer shooter set during the Vietnam War, part of the Red Orchestra series from Tripwire Interactive and Antimatter Games. Matches hold up to 64 players and pit American and allied forces against North Vietnamese and Viet Cong troops across jungle, village and city maps. Each side fights differently, with helicopters on one side and traps and tunnels on the other.

There is no story campaign; this is an online team game with deadly weapons, where a single hit often ends a life. It suits players who like realistic, team-focused shooters and are happy to communicate with a squad.
300380:
Road Redemption is a combat racing game in which you ride with a motorcycle gang and fight your way through races. While riding at full speed you swing weapons, kick rivals off their bikes and dodge traffic, earning money to upgrade between stages. The campaign is structured as a long run across the country, and failure sends you back to start again with your upgrades.

It can be played alone, and up to four people can ride together in split-screen co-op on one screen. It is a natural pick for anyone who misses the Road Rash games, and for groups wanting chaotic couch play.
464060:
RUINER is a fast top-down action shooter set in 2091 in Rengkok, a decaying cyberpunk city. You play a silent, masked man who is guided by a mysterious hacker as he fights through the city's corrupt system to rescue his kidnapped brother. Combat mixes guns, melee weapons, dashes and a shield, and it moves quickly.

It is a single-player game from the Polish studio Reikon Games, published by Devolver Digital, with violent, stylish combat and a short, linear campaign. It suits players who like twitchy arena fights, striking neon visuals and a challenge that rewards quick reactions and learning enemy patterns.
55230:
Saints Row: The Third is an open-world action game set in the city of Steelport, where the Third Street Saints, now celebrities, run into a criminal group called the Syndicate. You build up your gang, take over the city and complete missions full of gunfights, car chases and absurd set pieces, along with side activities that are deliberately silly.

The campaign can be played alone or online with a friend in co-op. It leans into comedy and spectacle rather than realism, so it suits players who want a loose, playful crime sandbox with lots of customization and little concern for keeping a straight face.
1438480:
Saviorless is a hand-drawn 2D adventure from Cuban studio Empty Head Games. A storyteller guides you toward the Smiling Islands, the home of the Saviors, a place that has always been out of reach in the tale he tells. Along the way the story shifts between characters, and the journey asks whether you can take the story into your own hands.

It is a single-player platformer with action and some puzzle-solving, carried by its detailed art and a story told partly through its narrator. It suits players who enjoy artistic, narrative-focused platformers and a moderate challenge, more than those looking for a long or combat-heavy game.
1141120:
Scarlet Hood and the Wicked Wood is a story-driven adventure about a young witch named Scarlet who has to guide a group of clumsy Munchkins through a dangerous forest. The wood belongs to a Black Witch named LeFaba, who does not welcome visitors, and things go badly. Scarlet soon discovers she is trapped in a loop, living the same day again and again.

Your choices shape what happens, and each loop gives you new knowledge to try something different. It is a single-player narrative game from Devespresso Games, suited to players who like dialogue choices, dark fairy tales and piecing together how to reach a better ending.
1037020:
ScourgeBringer is a fast roguelite action platformer. You play Kyhra, a warrior exploring a hostile, unknown place filled with ancient machines that guard a seal tied to her past and possibly to humanity's future. Rooms lock until you clear them, and you can dash and float freely through the air while slicing through enemies.

Each run builds a new layout, and you unlock lasting upgrades as you go. It is a single-player game with sharp pixel art and very quick combat, best suited to players who enjoy demanding roguelites and fluid movement, and who are happy to die often while improving.
40340:
Secret Files 2: Puritas Cordis is the sequel to the point-and-click adventure Secret Files: Tunguska. The world is suffering famine, floods, economic trouble and wars, and amid these disasters Nina Kalenkov and Max Gruber become tangled in a conspiracy tied to a secretive religious group that seems to know more about the coming crises than it should.

The game is played the classic way: exploring locations, talking to characters and combining items to solve puzzles. It is single-player and unhurried, suited to fans of traditional adventure games and of the first game who want to follow Nina and Max further.
40330:
Secret Files: Tunguska is a point-and-click mystery built around the real Tunguska event of 1908, when a huge explosion flattened forest across a remote part of Siberia. In the game, Nina Kalenkov finds her father, a scientist who studied the event, has vanished from his office, and her search with his colleague Max Gruber pulls them into a mystery that spans several countries.

You explore, collect and combine objects, and question characters to move the investigation along. It is a single-player adventure with a measured pace and no action, suited to players who enjoy classic puzzle-based adventures with a historical hook.
1227690:
Severed Steel is a fast first-person shooter built around movement. You play a one-armed fighter who flips, slides, wall-runs and dives through levels in slow motion, and nearly everything in the environment can be blasted apart, so walls and floors become openings. Firefights are short and acrobatic, encouraging stylish play rather than slow cover shooting.

It is a single-player game from Greylock Studio with a short campaign and plenty of challenge modes for replays, backed by a well-liked electronic soundtrack. It suits players who enjoy fast action, mastering movement and replaying levels to clear them more cleanly or quickly.
2500:
Shadowgrounds is a top-down shooter from Frozenbyte, the Finnish team later known for Trine. Aliens attack a human colony on Ganymede, a moon of Jupiter, and you fight through dark corridors and facilities armed with a growing set of weapons. Each gun can be upgraded with parts gathered during the campaign, and the lighting and explosions set a tense mood.

The campaign can be played alone or in local co-op on a single computer, sharing the keyboard or using gamepads. It suits fans of classic twin-stick and top-down shooters, and friends looking for some old-school alien blasting together.
3900:
Sid Meier's Civilization IV is a turn-based strategy game in which you guide a civilization from its first settlement through thousands of years of history. You found cities, research technologies, spread religions, build wonders and deal with rival leaders through trade, diplomacy or war. Victory can come through conquest, culture, space flight and other routes.

It is played alone against AI leaders or in multiplayer against friends, with a slow, thoughtful pace where a single game can last many hours. Widely considered one of the best games in the series, it suits strategy fans who enjoy long, deep campaigns and the classic one more turn feeling.
16810:
Built on the Civilization IV engine, Sid Meier's Civilization IV: Colonization remakes the 1994 game Colonization as a standalone release. You lead one of the European powers settling the New World, founding colonies, trading with the homeland and with native peoples, and building up an economy. The long-term goal is to break away from the crown and win a war of independence.

It is turn-based and can be played solo against AI or in multiplayer. Games focus more on trade, production and colony management than on research, so it suits strategy players who want a more focused, economic spin on the Civilization formula.
279900:
Soul Axiom is a first-person puzzle adventure with a strong story, made by Wales Interactive, the studio behind Master Reboot. It takes place in Elysia, a digital afterlife where memories are stored, and you explore its strange, haunting places to work out who you are and what went wrong there. Along the way you gain hand powers that let you change the world around you to solve puzzles.

It is a single-player game with multiple endings that depend on your path. It moves at an exploratory pace without demanding reflexes, and suits players who like mysterious sci-fi stories and environmental puzzles over combat.
1419160:
Souldiers is a pixel art action adventure from Spanish studio Retro Forge. A group of soldiers find themselves in a realm between life and death, and you fight to win your freedom while exploring a large interconnected map. At the start you choose one of three classes, which shapes how you approach combat throughout the adventure.

It combines metroidvania exploration, puzzle platforming and demanding combat inspired by Soulslike games. It is single-player and long, with tough enemies and bosses, so it suits players who like challenging retro-styled games and do not mind backtracking and learning attack patterns.
1602080:
Soulstice is a third-person action game set in a dark fantasy world. You control two sisters at once: Briar, a powerful warrior known as a Chimera, and Lute, the spirit of her sister bound to her, who supports her with defensive and supernatural abilities. Together they push through ruined lands overrun by monsters while their own story comes of age.

It is a single-player character-action game in the style of Devil May Cry or Bayonetta, with combos, multiple weapons and large boss battles. It suits players who enjoy mastering a deep combat system and learning to manage two characters at the same time.
1608700:
Soundfall is a dungeon-crawling game that blends loot-based shooting with rhythm. You explore a musical world, and timing your attacks, dashes and abilities to the beat makes you stronger. Enemies and levels react to the music, and there is a story campaign alongside a free play mode where you can use the built-in songs or bring in your own music files.

You can play alone or with as many as four people, together on one screen or online. Gear drops let you build your character over time. It suits rhythm game fans looking for something more action-oriented, and groups who want a relaxed, colorful co-op game.
214730:
Space Rangers HD: A War Apart is a remastered version of a well-loved Russian space game. The galaxy is under attack by the Dominators, a robotic force, and you are a ranger free to act as trader, pirate, hunter or defender. Travel between systems is turn-based, while space battles, text adventures and planetary strategy battles provide variety.

It is a large single-player game that lets you set your own goals and pace, mixing RPG progression, trading and many smaller game styles in one package. It suits patient players who enjoy open-ended sandboxes, reading, and a quirky mix of genres over a polished modern presentation.
2172580:
Spirit Mancer is a 2D action game in which you fight demons in a dangerous fantasy world. You use swords and guns in fast combat, and after beating enemies you can capture their spirits and later summon them to fight alongside you. The goal is to fight past waves of demons and defeat an evil queen.

It can be played alone or with a friend in local co-op on the same screen. Collecting and choosing which spirits to bring adds some strategy to the action. It suits players who enjoy retro-inspired action platformers and the fun of building a collection of monster allies.
3748520:
SPRAWL zero is a quick, aggressive first-person shooter inspired by the FPS games of the 2000s. It is set in a cyberpunk city falling apart under military control and the influence of fanatical cults, and you fight your way through it with a large arsenal of more than 40 weapons, implant augments and Gravity-Gloves that let you grab and throw objects and enemies.

It is a single-player game from MAETH, the developer of SPRAWL, published by Kwalee. Its pace is built around movement and gunplay rather than stealth. It suits players who miss classic shooters and want intense, weapon-heavy action in a gritty setting.
2055590:
Star Overdrive is an open-world action adventure set on an alien planet. You travel across the landscape on a hoverboard, building speed and pulling off tricks, and you use special powers to fight enemies, solve environmental puzzles and reach new areas. Exploration plays a large part, with the open world encouraging you to wander and discover.

It is a single-player game from Italian studio Caracal Games, published by Dear Villagers. Moving at speed is the main pleasure, mixed with lighter combat and puzzle-solving. It suits players who like freedom to explore and enjoy movement-focused games with some challenge.
252410:
SteamWorld Dig is a 2D mining adventure starring Rusty, a steam-powered robot who arrives in the small western town of Tumbleton to take over his uncle's mine. You dig downward through layers of rock, collect ore to sell in town, and spend the money on better tools and new abilities, uncovering what lies far underground as you go.

It is a single-player game that mixes platforming, light combat and puzzles, with metroidvania-style upgrades that open new paths. Its pace is steady and rewarding, and it is fairly short, so it suits players who enjoy a satisfying loop of digging, upgrading and exploring.
355790:
Styx: Shards of Darkness brings back the sharp-tongued goblin thief for a second outing, this time sending him into a city of dark elves on a job that proves more complicated than it looks. Levels are large, with several routes through each area, and you decide whether to slip by guards unseen or remove them quietly. Styx also gains new tools and powers, from traps to cloning tricks, to vary each approach.

This is a patient stealth game where planning, hiding and timing matter more than straight fights, which Styx usually loses. It can be played alone or with a friend in online co-op, and it suits players who enjoy careful sneaking and exploring big vertical spaces.
2920:
Sub Command is a naval simulation from Sonalysts that puts you in command of modern attack submarines, including American Seawolf and Los Angeles class boats and the Russian Akula. You hunt ships and other submarines using sonar, periscope and fire control stations, then launch torpedoes or missiles, and some missions even call for land attack strikes with cruise missiles. Two separate campaigns cover the different navies.

The game leans toward realism, so expect a learning curve and slow, tense hunts where reading sensor data matters more than reflexes. Alongside the single-player missions there is multiplayer, including co-op play. Sub Command suits players who like detailed military sims and the quiet cat-and-mouse feel of submarine warfare.
1525660:
Sunblaze is a precision platformer built around hundreds of short, handmade stages, each one a tight puzzle of hazards, spikes and moving parts. You guide a small heroine through these rooms, and the challenge is working out the right route and then pulling it off with exact jumps and dashes. Failure is frequent, but restarts are instant, so a hard room becomes a matter of trying again and again.

It is a single-player game aimed squarely at fans of demanding platformers in the vein of Celeste or Super Meat Boy. Levels are brief, which makes it easy to play in short sessions, though later stages can test patience. Anyone who enjoys mastering difficult movement will find plenty here.
3531260:
In Superhero Simulator you play a costumed hero who must also manage an ordinary life in a large open city. On one side you patrol the city, fight criminals and help people in trouble. On the other, heroics do not pay the bills, so you also hold down a job, keep up with rent and handle the daily needs that come with living in the city.

It is a single-player game that blends action with life simulation and light role-playing, so the pace swings between street fights and more relaxed routine tasks. It suits players who like sandbox games where balancing time and money is part of the challenge, and who enjoy the idea of a hero with everyday worries.
299680:
Tengami is a gentle adventure whose world is a pop-up book drawn from Japanese art and folklore. Everything is made of paper, and you move through it by turning pages, pulling tabs and folding scenes open or closed, which changes the landscape and reveals new paths. Puzzles are built into these paper mechanics, and the setting draws on traditional Japanese art, with shrines, forests and changing seasons.

It is a short single-player game with a calm pace and no combat, meant to be taken slowly and enjoyed for its look and sound as much as its puzzles. Tengami suits players who like quiet, artistic games and puzzles that reward observation rather than quick reactions.
1620720:
Grief, music and saying goodbye sit at the center of The Forest Quartet. You play as the spirit of a lead singer who has died, and you return to visit the three members of her old band. Each gets an act of their own, set in a world shaped by their feelings, and the goal is helping them face their loss so the band can perform one last concert together.

It is a single-player game that mixes environmental puzzles with some light action against a dark corruption tied to each character. The pace is steady and reflective, and the story carries much of the weight. It suits players looking for a short, emotional indie adventure with a strong musical theme.
251430:
The Inner World is a hand-drawn point-and-click adventure set in Asposia, an unusual world enclosed by an endless mass of earth. The winds that once blew through it have vanished, and Robert, a naive young court musician with a flute for a nose, leaves his sheltered life to find out why. Along the way he teams up with Laura, a quick-witted thief whose motives are not entirely clear.
