It plays like a classic adventure: talk to odd characters, collect items and combine them to solve puzzles, with a built-in hint system if you get stuck. It is single-player and relaxed in pace, with plenty of dry humor. The Inner World suits fans of traditional point-and-click games.
2131010:
The Land Beneath Us is a turn-based roguelite dungeon crawler set in Annwn, the underworld of Welsh myth. Each run sends you down through floors of enemies, and you work your way toward seven powerful lords while gathering upgrades called Soul-Tech and swapping between a range of weapons. Every move you make lets enemies move too, so positioning and chaining skill combos are the heart of the combat.

Although it is turn-based, it moves quickly, with short decisions rather than long pauses, so runs feel brisk. It is a single-player game, and since each run changes, it rewards replaying and experimenting with builds. It suits players who like tactical puzzles in combat and the steady progress of a roguelite.
1406850:
This side-scrolling action game is built around Liao Tianding, a Taiwanese folk hero remembered as an outlaw who stole from the wealthy and helped the poor. It is set in Taipei during the early twentieth century, when Taiwan was under Japanese rule, and the bustling streets and markets are drawn in a bold style inspired by comic books and traditional art.

In The Legend of Tianding, combat is fast and combo-driven, with a sash that lets Tianding grab enemy weapons and turn them against their owners, plus light role-playing upgrades. It is a single-player game with a steady difficulty curve and a story told in comic-style panels. The Legend of Tianding suits fans of stylish brawlers and historical settings.
1468380:
The Sundew is a pixel-art point-and-click adventure set in a bleak future. You play Anna Isobe, a police officer with cybernetic implants who has been left behind as the world moves on, and who stumbles into a conspiracy that reaches far beyond her own city. The story travels across several locations and asks you to make decisions that change how events unfold and how the story ends.

It plays like a traditional adventure, with conversations, item puzzles and investigation, at a measured pace suited to reading and exploring. It is a single-player game. The Sundew suits players who enjoy cyberpunk fiction and classic adventures in the style of the 1990s, especially those who like stories with choices that carry weight.
966670:
The Wanderer: Frankenstein's Creature retells Mary Shelley's novel from the point of view of the creature. You wake with no memory and no understanding of the world, and you set out on a journey across a landscape painted in soft watercolor style. As you meet people and react to them, your choices shape the creature's view of humanity and how the story ends.

It is a single-player narrative adventure with simple puzzles and musical sequences rather than combat, and the pace is slow and contemplative. Short in length, it works well in one or two sittings. It suits players who enjoy artistic, story-focused games and anyone curious to see a classic piece of literature from a new angle.
1557700:
This full-motion video adventure takes place in a French village during a pandemic lockdown. You follow a man troubled by strange recurring nightmares, and as he digs into their meaning he begins to suspect that the village he lives in is hiding something. The story is told through live-action footage with real actors, and your decisions guide where the investigation goes.

This single-player game works like an interactive film, so the focus is on watching scenes, picking options and piecing together the mystery rather than on reflexes or puzzles. The pace is slow and atmospheric. The World After suits players who enjoy FMV games, psychological mysteries and stories that unfold like a television drama.
1585440:
They Always Run is a 2D action platformer that mixes science fiction with the Wild West. You play Aiden, a mutant bounty hunter with three arms, who travels between planets chasing dangerous criminals with prices on their heads. His third arm is more than a gimmick: it gives him extra ways to block, grab and strike, and the sword-based combat builds on it as the story progresses.

It is a single-player game that mixes platforming, exploration and close-range fighting at a fairly brisk pace, with some tough encounters along the way. The tone is gritty but not grim, much like a frontier adventure set among the stars. It suits players who enjoy melee-focused action games with a distinct setting.
368430:
Played from a third-person view, Through the Woods takes place in the woods along Norway's western coast. A mother searches for her son, who has gone missing, and the night she spends among the trees draws her into a world of creatures taken from Norse folklore. The story is told largely through her recollections as she pushes deeper into the woods.

It is a single-player game built on atmosphere and tension rather than combat, since you mostly explore, hide and avoid threats with a flashlight in hand. The pace is slow and moody, and it can be finished in a few evenings. Through the Woods suits players who enjoy folk horror and walking-focused adventures.
617480:
Tower of Time is a story-driven role-playing game in which you lead a party of heroes down through a mysterious tower buried beneath the earth. Each floor holds puzzles, secrets and fights, and you upgrade your characters and their gear as you go deeper and learn more about where the tower came from. Its combat runs in real time but allows you to pause or slow it down to give orders.

That slowed combat makes it play like a tactics game, with plenty of thought about positioning and skill timing. It is single-player, and alternate modes offer a lighter role-playing ruleset and permanent death for a different challenge. It suits players who like classic party RPGs with tactical battles.
446800:
Transport Fever is a tycoon game about building a transport company from the age of steam to modern times. Starting in 1850, you lay rail lines, set up road routes and later add ships and aircraft to move passengers and goods between towns and industries. Each connection you build has to earn its keep, and as the decades pass new vehicles become available while older ones wear out.

It is a single-player management game with a calm pace, where most of the challenge lies in planning efficient networks and keeping the books in the black. There are campaign missions as well as a free play mode. Transport Fever suits players who enjoy model trains, logistics puzzles and long, slow-building sessions.
690640:
Trine 4: The Nightmare Prince returns the series to its side-on 2.5D style. Three heroes, Amadeus the wizard, Pontius the knight and Zoya the thief, set out to find a runaway prince whose bad dreams are spilling out into the world. Their journey passes through bright fairytale scenery full of physics puzzles and some combat with shadowy creatures.

Each hero has distinct abilities, and puzzles are solved by switching between them or combining their skills. Trine 4 can be played alone or with up to three friends in online or local split-screen co-op, where solutions often become more inventive. The pace is relaxed and the tone is warm, making it a good pick for couples, families and puzzle fans.
1911360:
Trinity Fusion is a sci-fi action roguelite with Metroidvania-style exploration. The multiverse is falling apart, and you play across three separate realities, each with its own version of the main character and its own style of fighting. Runs take you through dark, changing worlds, and between attempts you can merge traits from these parallel selves to build stronger and stranger combinations of weapons and powers.

Combat is fast and fluid, with dodges and quick attacks, so reflexes matter as much as planning your build. It is a single-player game, and the run-based structure makes it easy to play in short bursts while slowly unlocking new options. It suits fans of games like Dead Cells and Hades.
626610:
TT Isle of Man: Ride on the Edge is a motorcycle racing game built around the famous Tourist Trophy road race on the Isle of Man. Its centerpiece is the full Snaefell Mountain Course, a lap of more than 37 miles over public roads lined with walls, houses and hedges. Real riders and bikes from the event appear, and a career mode lets you work your way up.

The handling leans toward simulation, so it takes practice to keep a bike stable at high speed on narrow, bumpy roads. It offers single-player racing as well as online multiplayer against other riders. It suits motorcycle fans and racing players who want a serious challenge rather than an arcade experience.
292160:
UFO: Aftermath is a tactical strategy game set after an alien attack has devastated Earth. A strange biological mass is spreading across the planet, and you lead the survivors who try to push it back. On the world map you manage bases, research alien technology and decide where to send your teams. Missions then switch to an isometric 3D view, where your squad fights alien forces.

Battles run in real time but can be paused to give orders, so the pace is thoughtful rather than frantic. It is a single-player game in the tradition of the classic X-COM series. UFO: Aftermath suits strategy fans who enjoy managing a long campaign and planning squad tactics.
289500:
UFO: Aftershock is the sequel to UFO: Aftermath and carries on the story of humanity's fight against alien forces on a changed Earth. It combines a global strategy layer, where you expand territory, build bases, manage resources and research new gear, with tactical missions where your squad takes on hostile groups in detailed isolated maps. Compared with the first game, it adds more depth to both halves.

Combat is real-time with pause, so you can stop the action to plan moves and give orders. It is a single-player game with a long campaign and a fair amount of micromanagement. UFO: Aftershock suits strategy players who enjoy X-COM style games and want a broader campaign than the original.
1096410:
This story-driven game from Draw Distance takes place in the World of Darkness and draws on the fifth edition of the tabletop role-playing game. New York's nights are fought over by two vampire factions, the established Camarilla and the rebellious Anarchs. You choose one of three newly made vampires from different clans and try to find a place in this hostile society.

Vampire: The Masquerade - Coteries of New York plays like a visual novel, with illustrated scenes, plenty of reading and dialogue choices that affect relationships and outcomes. It is single-player, with almost no combat and a slow pace. It suits fans of the tabletop game and players who enjoy dark urban fantasy told through text.
1279630:
Vampire The Masquerade - Shadows of New York is a narrative game set in the World of Darkness. You play a newly turned vampire taken in by the Lasombra clan, a group that tolerates no failure. When a prominent figure in the city's vampire community is found dead, you are handed the case, and the investigation pulls you deeper into the politics of New York's undead.

Like Coteries of New York, it is presented as a visual novel, with illustrated scenes and choices that shape conversations and the ending. It is a single-player game focused on story, mood and dialogue rather than action. It suits players who like noir mysteries, dark fantasy and the Vampire: The Masquerade setting.
365770:
Volume is a stealth game from Bithell Games, whose earlier work includes Thomas Was Alone. It reimagines the Robin Hood story in a near future: Rob Locksley uses a simulation device to stream heists that show people how to steal from the rich and expose a corrupt ruler named Gisborne. Levels are clean, top-down virtual spaces where you dodge patrolling guards and collect gems.

Play is about patterns, sightlines and distractions, and you can retry instantly, so each stage becomes a neat stealth puzzle. It is single-player, and a built-in level editor lets players make and share their own stages. Volume suits players who prefer thoughtful stealth over action, and who like short, replayable levels.
1051410:
Close to interactive fiction in form, this is a narrative game. It follows several modern travelers on journeys around the world, and through their experiences it looks at what they are searching for, what worries them and what they hope to find. You make decisions at many points, shaping the course of each trip and how each character changes.

It is a single-player game that is almost entirely text, supported by illustrations, so Wanderlust Travel Stories plays like a choose-your-path book. There is no combat and no time pressure. Wanderlust Travel Stories suits readers, people who love travel writing and players looking for a calm, thoughtful game to enjoy at their own speed.
395570:
Three dwarven astronauts are the heroes of We Are The Dwarves, a tactical adventure played in real time. In their universe, stars sit inside stone, and the trio head into the depths to find new light for their people. Each dwarf has a distinct role and skill set, and you guide them through hostile caverns full of creatures that punish careless moves.

Combat runs in real time but can be paused or slowed to give orders, so it rewards planning, stealth and careful use of abilities. It is a single-player game with a stiff difficulty level. It suits players who enjoy squad tactics in the style of Commandos or Baldur's Gate and do not mind a challenge.
2296990:
We Were Here Expeditions: The FriendShip is a short, standalone entry in the We Were Here series of co-op puzzle games. Two players set out on a voyage together, each seeing different parts of a puzzle, and the only way through is to describe what you see and work out the solution together. The tone is lighter than earlier entries, built around a friendship-testing excursion.

It is strictly a two-player online co-op game with no solo mode, and communication by voice chat is essential. Sessions are brief, so it can be finished in an evening, and puzzles change between rounds for replay. It suits pairs of friends or partners who enjoy escape-room style puzzles and talking things through.
226120:
Weird Worlds: Return to Infinite Space, from the small studio Digital Eel, is a roguelike about exploring space. Each game is a short expedition in a randomly generated part of the galaxy, where you pilot a starship, visit star systems, meet odd alien races, find artifacts and recruit allies, all while racing against a time limit before you must return home. Starship battles break out when encounters turn hostile.

A single game takes roughly half an hour, so it fits short sessions and shows something new each time. It is a single-player game with a light, quirky tone and simple controls. Weird Worlds suits players who like quick space adventures and the replay value of a roguelike.
1342620:
Werewolf: The Apocalypse - Heart of the Forest is a narrative role-playing game set in the Bialowieza Forest, one of Europe's oldest stretches of wild woodland, on the border of Poland and Belarus. You play Maia, a young woman who travels there to look into her family history, and soon discovers ties to Garou, werewolves who guard the natural world, and to a growing rage of her own.

It is a single-player game told mostly through text and illustrations, where your choices and how you manage Maia's emotions shape the story and its endings. It is based on the classic tabletop role-playing game. It suits fans of interactive fiction, folklore and slow, character-focused stories.
301560:
White Night is a survival horror game set in the 1930s, presented in stark black and white. After a car crash on a lonely road, the main character takes refuge in an old mansion and becomes trapped there. Inside, he uncovers the house's dark past, while shadowy ghosts lurk in the dark. Light is your main defense, so matches and lamps are precious.

Puzzles revolve around light and shadow, and the game pairs exploration with tense moments of avoiding threats rather than fighting them. It is a single-player experience with a slow, noir-flavored pace and a strong visual style. White Night suits players who enjoy classic haunted-house horror and a moody, film-noir atmosphere.
2820:
X3: Terran Conflict is a space simulation set in the year 2938, after Earth has finally made contact with the alien races of the X setting. Trade flourishes, but friction and open conflict follow. You start with a single ship and are free to trade goods, take on missions, fight pirates, explore sectors and eventually run fleets and factories across the galaxy.

It is a single-player sandbox with a steep learning curve, where much of the play happens through menus and long-term planning as well as in the cockpit. The pace is slow and open-ended. X3: Terran Conflict suits players who want a detailed space economy and a game they can sink many hours into.
888530:
Yaga is an action role-playing game rooted in Slavic folklore. You play Ivan, a blacksmith with one hand and a talent for bad luck, who is sent on a string of impossible tasks by the tzar. As he travels through villages and forests filled with creatures from old tales, the witch Baba Yaga keeps an eye on his fate. The story is narrated in rhyming verse.

Combat centers on Ivan's hammer and tools he forges himself, and how you treat the people you meet changes how the story plays out. It is a single-player game with a hand-drawn look and shifting levels, so replays vary. Yaga suits players who like action RPGs with folklore and humor.
308420:
Ziggurat is a first-person action roguelike in which you play an apprentice wizard sent into a randomly built dungeon as a final test. Armed with a wand, spellbooks, staffs and alchemy weapons, you fight through rooms full of monsters, collect perks as you level up and face bosses at the end of each floor. Since the layout changes every time, no two runs look the same.

Combat is fast and arcade-like, with lots of dodging and a steady stream of projectiles, and a run can be finished in under an hour. It is a single-player game that rewards learning enemies and trying new builds. Ziggurat suits players who like quick shooters with roguelike progression.
1472560:
I Am Fish is a physics-based adventure from Bossa Studios, the team behind I Am Bread. A group of fish friends are separated and taken from their home, and each one has to find a way back to the ocean. That means rolling a fishbowl through houses and streets, flopping across land and swimming through pipes and rivers, with each fish having its own way of moving.

The controls are deliberately tricky, so much of the fun and frustration comes from steering a fragile creature through obstacles. It is a single-player game with a light, comic tone and levels that can be retried quickly. It suits players who enjoy quirky physics puzzles and slapstick challenges.
518699:
Mortal Kombat 11 Ultimate is the complete edition of NetherRealm Studios' fighting game. It includes the base game, the Aftermath story expansion and both Kombat Packs, bringing the full roster of fighters together in one package. The cinematic story mode continues the series' saga, with the keeper of time, Kronika, rewriting history and pulling characters from different eras into conflict with their own pasts.

Fights are one-on-one, with combos, special moves, gory finishers and a detailed system for customizing each character's gear and abilities. You can play alone through the story and towers or face others in local and online multiplayer. It suits fighting game fans of all levels, from casual players to competitive ones.
